title: China’s AI models have Trump’s AI world at war with itself

paragraphs.text: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
paragraphs.translation: 這是最初出現在我們每週 AI 時事通訊《The Algorithm》中的報導。欲搶先在收件匣中閱讀此類故事，請點擊此處訂閱。

paragraphs.text: Over the weekend, several current and former advisors to President Donald Trump on AI publicly lobbed insults at the country’s leading AI companies. David Sacks, the president’s AI and crypto “czar” until March, branded Anthropic’s models as “lobotomized” and “woke.” Emil Michael, a top Pentagon official, called OpenAI’s new head of strategic futures a “supreme village idiot.”
paragraphs.translation: 上週末，幾位川普總統現任與前任 AI 顧問公開向該國領先的 AI 公司惡言相向。今年三月前的總統 AI 與加密貨幣「沙皇」大衛·薩克斯（David Sacks）將 Anthropic 的模型標榜為「被切除腦葉的」且「覺醒文化的」。五角大廈高官埃米爾·邁克爾（Emil Michael）稱 OpenAI 的新戰略未來負責人為「頂級村愚」。

paragraphs.text: It began because no one can agree on what to do about Kimi, a free, open source model that Chinese AI company Moonshot launched last week. It appears to rival the intelligence of models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which are very much not free.
paragraphs.translation: 這一切的起因是，對於如何處理 Kimi，大家無法達成共識。Kimi 是中國 AI 公司月之暗面（Moonshot）上週推出的免費開源模型。它的智慧程度似乎足以與 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的模型匹敵，而後者絕非免費。

paragraphs.text: Kimi and other Chinese models like it pose a real problem for Trump. And they’re dividing the top AI strategists in his orbit into factions. Every time a new smart, free model from China like Kimi gets released, US companies see less reason to fork out money to access models from Anthropic or OpenAI. Given that enthusiasm for these and other AI companies is driving an outsized share of economic growth, China’s AI models create both economic and political problems for the president. They are “a threat for an administration that really doesn’t want more economic bad news,” Anton Leicht, a fellow at the Carnegie Endowment, wrote on X. They’ve already rattled US stocks.
paragraphs.translation: Kimi 和其他類似的中國模型對川普構成了一個真正的難題。它們正將他周邊的頂尖 AI 策略家分裂成不同派系。每當像 Kimi 這樣新型、聰明且免費的中國模型發布時，美國公司就越沒有理由花大錢去購買 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的模型。鑑於對這些及其他 AI 公司的熱情正推動著不成比例的經濟增長，中國的 AI 模型為總統製造了經濟與政治上的雙重問題。卡內基國際和平基金會研究員安東·萊希特（Anton Leicht）在 X 上寫道，它們是「一個確實不希望看到更多經濟壞消息的政府的威脅」。它們已經引發了美國股市的動盪。

paragraphs.text: What is Trump to do? First, consider that this is all happening just a week after New York imposed the country’s first state ban on new data centers. There is growing distrust of AI companies, and I imagine a not-insignificant share of Americans would have little sympathy for OpenAI or Anthropic as they fend off cheaper competitors, and would say it’s not the government’s job to protect their interests.
paragraphs.translation: 川普該怎麼辦？首先，考慮到這一切發生在紐約實施全美首個州級新數據中心禁令的一週之後。大眾對 AI 公司的信任度日益降低，我猜測有相當比例的美國人對 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 抵禦更廉價的競爭對手幾乎沒有同情心，且會認為保護他們的利益並非政府的職責。

paragraphs.text: On this point, they’d see a sliver of agreement (and really just a sliver) with David Sacks, who on July 19 criticized top AI companies that “want the government to eliminate their open source competition.” He has also argued that Chinese AI models have become popular because they come with fewer restrictions on how people can use them (putting aside the built-in state censorship).
paragraphs.translation: 在這一點上，他們會與大衛·薩克斯有一絲共鳴（真的只有一絲），後者在 7 月 19 日批評頂尖 AI 公司「希望政府消除他們的開源競爭對手」。他也主張中國的 AI 模型之所以變得流行，是因為它們對人們的使用方式限制較少（暫且不論其內建的國家審查）。

paragraphs.text: Sacks, however, is out of a job. He no longer has a formal role advising Trump, and his position that more open AI is better has been largely replaced in the administration by one that sees a larger role for government intervention. The thinking behind this view is that because AI models have gotten strong enough to pose threats to national security, the government must control how they’re used.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，薩克斯已經失業了。他不再擔任川普的正式顧問職位，而他那種「越開放的 AI 越好」的立場，在現任政府中已大幅被認為政府應加強干預的觀點所取代。這種觀點背後的思考是，由於 AI 模型已強大到足以對國家安全構成威脅，政府必須控制它們的使用方式。

paragraphs.text: This position has fueled the new White House review process that aims to vet AI models’ security before they’re released. Dean Ball, a former Trump AI advisor who now works for OpenAI, criticized it over the weekend as a “de facto licensing regime for frontier AI.” Ball predicted Trump may solve his Chinese open source problem with a bit of soft power, perhaps by making US companies afraid to use models like Kimi. That drew a response from Michael, who, with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, has been the agency’s main liaison with AI companies. Michael called Ball the AI industry’s “supreme village idiot,” bristling at the suggestion that the government would quietly strong-arm companies rather than, as Michael put it, go through “the democratic process not some Deep State scheme.”
paragraphs.translation: 這種立場催生了新的白宮審查程序，旨在模型發布前審核其安全性。前川普 AI 顧問、現職於 OpenAI 的迪恩·鮑爾（Dean Ball）上週末批評這是一個「實質上的尖端 AI 許可制度」。鮑爾預測川普可能會用一些軟實力來解決中國開源模型的問題，或許是讓美國公司不敢使用像 Kimi 這樣的模型。這引起了邁克爾的回應，他與國防部長皮特·海格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）一直是該機構與 AI 公司的主要聯絡人。邁克爾稱鮑爾為 AI 業界的「頂級村愚」，並對那種認為政府會悄悄施壓公司而非（如邁克爾所言）通過「民主程序而非某種深層政府陰謀」的說法感到憤怒。

paragraphs.text: Left out of the conversation has been how a model like Kimi got so good in the first place. For much of the Biden administration and even the beginning of Trump’s second administration, keeping China from getting top chips was a priority. Those export controls have loosened—Trump made the controversial decision to allow Nvidia to sell more chips to China, in exchange for the US government taking a cut—and the government has alleged that some chip smuggling has taken place. But China nonetheless has limited computing power, and it’s not clear what chips the company behind Kimi used to train the model.
paragraphs.translation: 討論中被遺漏的是，像 Kimi 這樣的模型最初是如何變得如此強大的。在拜登政府的大部分時間，甚至在川普第二任期的開始，阻止中國獲取頂尖晶片一直是優先事項。這些出口管制已經放寬——川普做出了讓 NVIDIA 向中國出售更多晶片的爭議性決定，以換取美國政府從中抽成——政府還指控發生了一些晶片走私。但儘管如此，中國的運算能力有限，目前尚不清楚 Kimi 背後的公司使用什麼晶片來訓練該模型。

paragraphs.text: It’s possible that the process involved some distillation, a practice in which AI models are trained on the outputs of existing AI models. OpenAI and Anthropic have long complained that Chinese AI companies do this, and they have requested government help to put a stop to it. In April, they got it, when the Trump administration announced a series of efforts to curb the practice.
paragraphs.translation: 這個過程可能涉及某種「蒸餾」（distillation），這是一種利用現有 AI 模型的輸出來訓練新 AI 模型的做法。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 長期以來一直抱怨中國 AI 公司這樣做，並請求政府幫助制止這種行為。今年四月，他們得到了幫助，當時川普政府宣佈了一系列旨在遏制這種做法的措施。

paragraphs.text: But Kimi is out there and free, and it is nearly as good as the Anthropic model the US government deemed so powerful that it was briefly shut down because it threatened national security. The weekend’s sparring suggests many in Trump’s orbit see that as a wake-up call. But nobody can agree on what for.
paragraphs.translation: 但 Kimi 已經問世且免費，而且它幾乎與美國政府認為過於強大、曾因威脅國家安全而短暫關閉的 Anthropic 模型一樣出色。週末的口角暗示，川普周邊的許多人將此視為一記警鐘。但沒有人能就這警鐘意味著什麼達成一致。

paragraphs.text: As tools like Claude Code get better, more and more developers are happy to hand off coding tasks to them. The way software gets built has changed for good.
